newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bottlers Sidel, Gebo to merge.
newsitem.headline: French bottlers Sidel, Gebo to merge.

text.p: French firms Sidel and Gebo said on Wednesday said they would merge in a bid to increase their clout in the world beverage bottling market, creating a group with annual turnover of 4.6 billion francs.
Sidel is a leader in plastic bottle-making machines while Gebo specialises in bottling assembly lines.
The merger is being carried out on a basis of 21 Sidel shares for 10 Gebo shares. The agreement will be put to shareholders at the end of October.
Profits would have been around 400 million francs before tax increases announced by France's new leftist government this week targeting companies.
The measures aimed at plugging France's deficit in the runup to monetary union will wipe some 20 to 25 million francs from profits.
For 1996, proforma turnover would have been 3.62 billion francs. Sidel's 1996 net profit was 263 million francs and Gebo's was 58.3 million.
The merger should have an earnings positive effect on 1998 earnings per share, Pierre Schoen, head of Gebo, told a news conference.
The deal is aimed at tapping an expected growth in the plastic packaging market for beer.
